novelty_scope: Compared with the inspected implementations in this repository. No claim of global scientific novelty or exhaustive novelty across every sibling method.

candidates.hypothesis: Candidate-edge relative strike in the fitted damage zone
layers: Cached numerical feature stack, band 14 short name tmi
candidates.signature: Gaussian scalar derivatives supply an axial magnetic-edge tangent and coherence. A fitted interaction uses cos(2*(candidate strike - primary strike)), distance and mapped component length.
candidates.why_missing_faults: A secondary strand may offset magnetized units even when it has no mapped surface trace. Its candidate strike can be consistent with the locally measured anatomy of visible-host systems.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Existing phi describes the offset vector from a host, not a candidate strand's orientation. This adds catalogue-independent candidate-to-host strike evidence without copying a prior raster.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Magnetized dikes, lithologic contacts and airborne leveling stripes
candidates.expected_improvement: Highest of these four, but unquantified and uncertain
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; CPU only, cached stack restored automatically
candidates.obtainability: Verified: all five public bridge parts and the assembled stack passed hash checks; official origin remains unauthenticated

layers: Visible catalogue strike tensors at two smoothing scales
candidates.signature: Axial turning difference and local curvature modify an empirically fitted cross-strike zone; no predetermined stress-lobe angle.
candidates.why_missing_faults: Bends could concentrate secondary deformation beside a host rather than on its already mapped centerline.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Current features include one tensor coherence and strike, but no multi-scale turning field. This is not the previously proposed endpoint-lobe test.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Cartographic smoothing and contour-following trace generalization
candidates.obtainability: All required cached data are present
candidates.status: NOT RUN; three-experiment cap and stop gate honored

layers: Nearest two distinct visible fault components
candidates.signature: Joint relative distances and host-strike disagreement identify overlap between empirically fitted damage contributions from distinct mapped strands.
candidates.why_missing_faults: Short linking strands may occupy overlap between neighboring host zones rather than the maximum of a nearest-host-only halo.
candidates.difference_from_repo: The existing intensity uses a single nearest component. This proposes an explicit two-host interaction, not another isotropic dilation.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: A mapped lithologic boundary situated between unrelated structural lineaments
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; distinct-host neighbor retrieval needs careful tests
candidates.obtainability: All required cached data are present
candidates.status: NOT RUN; three-experiment cap and stop gate honored

candidates.signature: An empirical transition/heterogeneity indicator conditions secondary-strand distance and orientation rather than assuming a uniform fault-wide handedness.
candidates.why_missing_faults: Changes in recorded motion might identify zones where distributed transfer between normal and strike-slip strands occurs.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Previous work tested a single nearest sense flag; it did not test spatial changes in sense along a host.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Inconsistent catalogue attribution and record boundaries
candidates.expected_improvement: Lower; attribute precision and matching are limiting
candidates.implementation_cost: Low after a reliable visible-only attribute join
candidates.obtainability: The supplied bridge CSV is present and hash verified; official v2 metadata and CC BY 4.0 license were retrieved
candidates.status: NOT RUN; single-sense ablation is E3, not validation of this transition hypothesis
